title: The Real Option Type
story: You built your own Option type in L2. But the XIOM compiler has a secret built-in type called Option[T] waiting for you — and it's faster, safer, and already wired into the entire language. Time to meet the real deal!
why: XIOM's built-in Option[T] is the official way to represent 'something or nothing' — it's recognized by the compiler, all standard library functions use it, and it powers error-free handling of missing values.
analogy: Option is like a box that might be empty. You always check inside before using what's there — and the language won't let you skip the check.
try_it: Change `score` to `None` — does the output change? Then create a `Some("hello")` string Option and match on it, printing the greeting or "No greeting".
tips: Use `Some(value)` to wrap a value in Option — the compiler infers the inner type
Declare a None with a type annotation: `let x: Option[Int] = None;` so XIOM knows the type
Match always needs both arms — `Some(v) =>` and `None =>` — the compiler enforces this
common_mistakes: Writing `let x = None;` without a type annotation — the compiler can't guess what type of None you want
Forgetting the second match arm — XIOM requires exhaustive matching, you can't leave out `None`
Trying to use the value directly like `score + 10` without unwrapping through match
